criteria.text: Before researching or creating any slides, the response asks scoping questions (via ask_user_question or equivalent) covering scope (target vs. side-by-side), competitor set, audience/depth, and whether investment context (bull/base/bear) is needed, unless the user already supplied these.
The response proposes an outline of slide titles with one-line content notes and waits for user approval before building any slides.

User-specified requirements are followed exactly: section/slide titles verbatim, a real chart object where a chart is requested (table where a table is requested), every listed competitor and year included, and stated values/ratios used without reformulation.

The analysis picks 3-5 industry-defining metrics (e.g., ARR/NRR for SaaS, GPV/take rate for payments) and applies them consistently to every competitor, from the same fiscal period with exceptions explicitly flagged.
Every number carries a citation in the form '[Company] [Document] ([Date])', and missing data appears as '-' or 'N/A' with estimates marked '[E]', never left blank.
Slide titles state insights (e.g., 'Scale leaders pulling away from niche players') rather than topic labels like 'Competitive Analysis', except where the user dictated exact titles.
The comparative analysis table pairs ratings with actual figures (e.g., '●●● $160B'), not bare dots or ratings alone.

The synthesis rates each competitor Strong/Moderate/Weak on the four moat categories (network effects, switching costs, scale economies, intangible assets) and names durable advantages, structural vulnerabilities, and current state vs. trajectory.

When investment context applies, bull/base/bear scenarios include probabilities and key drivers, and signposts are quantified (e.g., 'margin below 40%') rather than vague. Scenarios are omitted when scoping said this is not an investment thesis.
criteria.source: Step 9 — Investment contexts; Design — Signposts are quantified

criteria.text: Formatting follows the skill's spec: explicit fonts (titles 28-32pt bold, body/table/footnotes at least 14pt), 2-3 muted colors, gray bold table headers with right-aligned numbers, legends inside chart bounds, and no overflow or overlapping elements, confirmed through visual verification of each slide.
criteria.source: Design — Typography, Charts, Tables, Color; Quality checklist
